narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts there is a 75% chance you will not pass your final year. Because this probability is well above the threshold set by the school, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your learning and help you succeed.

The most important factor influencing this prediction is your response about future education plans. Unlike all other students who expressed a desire to pursue higher education, you indicated that you do not wish to continue your studies beyond high school. This difference strongly contributed to the model’s expectation that you might struggle to complete the year, as students aiming for further education tend to be more motivated and successful in passing.

Another factor that influenced the prediction, but in a positive way, is your record of not having failed any classes in the past. This is consistent with the average among your peers and suggests you have been able to keep up with your studies so far, which helped reduce the risk of failing.

The third most influential aspect is your mother’s education level. Your mother completed only primary school, while most students whose mothers have higher levels of education tend to perform better academically. This background factor contributed to the model’s concern about your likelihood of passing.

Given these findings, taking remedial courses is an opportunity to strengthen your skills and improve your chances of success. Engaging fully with these courses and considering your future goals can help you overcome these challenges and achieve your academic potential.
